card: Parallelizes BIP 157/158 compact block filter evaluation during wallet fast rescans using a worker thread pool. Introduces the -walletpar configuration option to control concurrency, defaulting to auto-detecting core count capped at 8 threads. Fast wallet rescans currently evaluate block filters sequentially on a single core, leaving other cores idle when scanning long chain intervals. On mainnet benchmarks scanning 200,000 blocks, rescan duration dropped from 272 seconds to 34.8 seconds with 8 threads (an ~7.8x speedup). Block reading, matching, and keypool top-ups remain serialized on the main thread, while in-flight negative filter verdicts are re-checked against newly derived descriptor scripts.
changed_since_previous: Refined progress logging and saving cadence during scanning, and extended functional tests in wallet_fast_rescan.py to explicitly test both serial and parallel scan modes.
evidence: Author's mainnet benchmark scanning 200,000 blocks: master took 272.2s, while this PR took 131.2s with 2 threads and 34.8s with 8 threads (~7.8x speedup) with no observed change in memory usage.
problem: Fast wallet rescans check compact block filters sequentially on a single thread. Rescanning large block ranges or restoring wallets on multi-core systems leaves available CPU cores idle and makes rescans take several minutes.

risk.why: A race condition or indexing bug in filter checking or incremental script patching could cause blocks to be falsely skipped during rescan, leaving the wallet with missing transactions and incorrect balances.

scope_notes: Significant refactor of wallet scan pipeline logic in src/wallet/scan.{h,cpp} introducing parallel worker dispatching, queue batching, and incremental filter verdict patching.
summary: Parallelizes BIP 157/158 compact block filter evaluation during wallet fast rescans using a bounded worker thread pool. Adds the -walletpar configuration option (defaulting to auto-detected CPU cores up to 8 threads) to control wallet concurrency. Block reading and wallet state modifications remain serialized on the main thread, while filter checks are batched and scheduled in parallel, and keypool top-ups re-check in-flight non-matching blocks only against newly added descriptor scripts.
